cards.front: Why does multiple myeloma cause punched-out lytic lesions and hypercalcemia?
cards.back: Myeloma cells activate **osteoclasts** (through **RANKL** and **IL-6**) and suppress osteoblasts. Bone is destroyed and calcium is released, but little new bone forms. So **alkaline phosphatase is usually normal** and a **bone scan** often misses the lesions.
cards.back_pt: As células do mieloma ativam os **osteoclastos** (via **RANKL** e **IL-6**) e suprimem os osteoblastos. O osso é destruído e libera cálcio, mas forma-se pouco osso novo. Por isso a **fosfatase alcalina costuma ser normal** e a **cintilografia óssea** muitas vezes não mostra as lesões.

cards.front: How do Bence Jones proteins damage the kidney in multiple myeloma?
cards.back: Free **light chains** are filtered and bind **uromodulin** (Tamm-Horsfall protein). They form dense **casts** that block the distal tubules (**myeloma cast nephropathy**). The standard urine dipstick detects mainly albumin, so it can **miss light chains**.
cards.back_pt: As **cadeias leves** livres são filtradas e se ligam à **uromodulina** (proteína de Tamm-Horsfall). Formam **cilindros** densos que obstruem os túbulos distais (**nefropatia por cilindros do mieloma**). A fita reagente de urina detecta principalmente albumina, por isso pode **não detectar as cadeias leves**.

cards.front: How does Waldenström macroglobulinemia differ from multiple myeloma?
cards.back: It is a **lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma** that makes monoclonal **IgM**. The large pentamer causes **hyperviscosity**: blurred vision with dilated retinal veins, headache and mucosal bleeding. Cold-reacting IgM can cause **Raynaud phenomenon**. Unlike myeloma, there are **no lytic bone lesions**.
cards.back_pt: É um **linfoma linfoplasmocítico** que produz **IgM** monoclonal. O pentâmero grande causa **hiperviscosidade**: visão turva com veias retinianas dilatadas, cefaleia e sangramento de mucosas. A IgM que reage ao frio pode causar **fenômeno de Raynaud**. Diferente do mieloma, **não há lesões ósseas líticas**.

cards.front: Which clinical clues suggest AL amyloidosis from a plasma cell clone?
cards.back: **Macroglossia**, **periorbital purpura** (fragile vessels), **nephrotic syndrome**, restrictive cardiomyopathy, peripheral or autonomic neuropathy, and hepatomegaly. The deposits are **light-chain** fragments, often lambda, that stain with **Congo red** (apple-green birefringence).
cards.back_pt: **Macroglossia**, **púrpura periorbitária** (vasos frágeis), **síndrome nefrótica**, cardiomiopatia restritiva, neuropatia periférica ou autonômica e hepatomegalia. Os depósitos são fragmentos de **cadeias leves**, frequentemente lambda, que coram com **vermelho Congo** (birrefringência verde-maçã).

cards.front: Which mutation links polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia and primary myelofibrosis?
cards.back: **JAK2 V617F**: a gain-of-function mutation in the **tyrosine kinase** used by the EPO, TPO and G-CSF receptors, so cells grow **without the growth factor**. It is in almost all PV and about half of ET and PMF.
cards.back_pt: **JAK2 V617F**: mutação de ganho de função na **tirosina quinase** usada pelos receptores de EPO, TPO e G-CSF, de modo que as células crescem **sem o fator de crescimento**. Está presente em quase todos os casos de PV e em cerca de metade dos casos de TE e de MFP.

cards.front: What are the classic clinical features of polycythemia vera?
cards.back: High **red cell mass** with **low EPO**. Headache and facial plethora, **itching after a warm bath** (histamine from basophils and mast cells), **erythromelalgia** (burning, red hands and feet), splenomegaly, and **thrombosis**, including **Budd-Chiari syndrome**.
cards.back_pt: **Massa eritrocitária** alta com **EPO baixa**. Cefaleia e pletora facial, **prurido após banho quente** (histamina de basófilos e mastócitos), **eritromelalgia** (mãos e pés vermelhos e em queimação), esplenomegalia e **trombose**, incluindo **síndrome de Budd-Chiari**.

cards.front: How do you tell CML from a leukemoid reaction?
cards.back: Both show very high neutrophil counts with immature forms. **CML**: **low LAP** score, **basophilia**, splenomegaly, and **BCR-ABL** (t(9;22)). **Leukemoid reaction** (severe infection, stress): **high LAP**, toxic granulation, **Döhle bodies**, no basophilia.
cards.back_pt: Ambos mostram neutrofilia muito alta com formas imaturas. **LMC**: escore de **FAL baixo**, **basofilia**, esplenomegalia e **BCR-ABL** (t(9;22)). **Reação leucemoide** (infecção grave, estresse): **FAL alta**, granulações tóxicas, **corpúsculos de Döhle**, sem basofilia.

cards.front: What are the hallmarks of myelodysplastic syndromes?
cards.back: A clonal stem cell disorder of older adults or after **chemotherapy/radiotherapy**. **Cytopenias despite a usually hypercellular marrow** (ineffective hematopoiesis), **dysplasia** (**ring sideroblasts**, bilobed **pseudo-Pelger-Huët** neutrophils), and **fewer than 20% blasts**. It can progress to **AML**.
cards.back_pt: Doença clonal da célula-tronco em idosos ou após **quimioterapia/radioterapia**. **Citopenias apesar de medula geralmente hipercelular** (hematopoese ineficaz), **displasia** (**sideroblastos em anel**, neutrófilos bilobados **pseudo-Pelger-Huët**) e **menos de 20% de blastos**. Pode evoluir para **LMA**.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man comes for a routine check-up. He feels well and has no bone pain. Total serum protein is mildly elevated. Serum protein electrophoresis shows a narrow band in the gamma region, and immunofixation identifies a monoclonal IgG kappa protein. Hemoglobin is 14.2 g/dL, serum calcium is 9.4 mg/dL, and creatinine is 0.9 mg/dL. A skeletal survey shows no bone lesions. A bone marrow biopsy shows 4% clonal plasma cells. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
choices: Multiple myeloma
Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance
Waldenström macroglobulinemia
Reactive polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia
AL amyloidosis
questions.explanation: An **M protein** with **fewer than 10% clonal plasma cells** and **no end-organ damage** (normal calcium, kidney function, hemoglobin and bones) is **MGUS**. Multiple myeloma is the most tempting choice, but it needs a larger plasma cell clone (10% or more) plus end-organ damage such as **CRAB** features, which are absent here. Waldenström makes IgM, not IgG, and a reactive process gives a broad polyclonal band, not a narrow spike. MGUS can progress to myeloma, so patients are followed over time.
questions.explanation_pt: Uma **proteína M** com **menos de 10% de plasmócitos clonais** e **sem lesão de órgão-alvo** (cálcio, função renal, hemoglobina e ossos normais) é **GMSI**. O mieloma múltiplo é a opção mais tentadora, mas exige um clone maior de plasmócitos (10% ou mais) e lesão de órgão-alvo, como as alterações **CRAB**, ausentes aqui. A macroglobulinemia de Waldenström produz IgM, não IgG, e um processo reativo gera uma banda policlonal larga, não um pico estreito. A GMSI pode evoluir para mieloma, por isso o paciente é acompanhado ao longo do tempo.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man has 2 months of fatigue, night sweats, weight loss and early satiety. The spleen is palpable 12 cm below the left costal margin. WBC count is 160,000/mm3 with neutrophils at all stages of maturation, many myelocytes, increased basophils and eosinophils, and 2% blasts. Platelets are 520,000/mm3. The leukocyte alkaline phosphatase score is low. Which molecular mechanism best explains this disease?
choices: Fusion gene that encodes a constitutively active tyrosine kinase
Point mutation that constitutively activates JAK2
Fusion protein that blocks retinoic acid-dependent differentiation
Translocation that places BCL2 under the immunoglobulin heavy-chain promoter
Translocation that causes overexpression of cyclin D1
questions.explanation: Massive splenomegaly, a left-shifted leukocytosis with **basophilia** and a **low LAP** score point to **chronic myeloid leukemia**. The **t(9;22) Philadelphia chromosome** creates the **BCR-ABL** fusion gene, which encodes a constitutively active **tyrosine kinase** that drives myeloid proliferation; tyrosine kinase inhibitors such as imatinib block it. **JAK2 V617F** is the most tempting choice because it also causes a myeloproliferative neoplasm, but it is typical of PV, ET and primary myelofibrosis, not CML. PML-RARA t(15;17) causes acute promyelocytic leukemia.
questions.explanation_pt: Esplenomegalia volumosa, leucocitose com desvio à esquerda, **basofilia** e escore de **FAL baixo** indicam **leucemia mieloide crônica**. A **t(9;22), cromossomo Filadélfia**, cria o gene de fusão **BCR-ABL**, que codifica uma **tirosina quinase** constitutivamente ativa que estimula a proliferação mieloide; inibidores de tirosina quinase como o imatinibe a bloqueiam. A **JAK2 V617F** é a opção mais tentadora, pois também causa neoplasia mieloproliferativa, mas é típica de PV, TE e mielofibrose primária, não de LMC. A PML-RARA t(15;17) causa leucemia promielocítica aguda.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man has headaches and dizziness. He reports intense itching after hot showers and episodes of burning pain and redness in his toes. He has never smoked and takes no medications. His face is ruddy, and the spleen tip is palpable. Hemoglobin is 19.8 g/dL, hematocrit is 60%, WBC count is 13,000/mm3, and platelets are 610,000/mm3. Oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Serum erythropoietin is low. Which mechanism best explains his high hematocrit?
choices: Erythropoietin release in response to chronic hypoxemia
Erythropoietin secretion by a renal tumor
Growth factor-independent proliferation of a myeloid stem cell clone
Reduced plasma volume from dehydration
Androgen stimulation of erythropoietin production
questions.explanation: Itching after bathing, erythromelalgia, splenomegaly, high counts in all three lines, **normal oxygen saturation** and **low EPO** point to **polycythemia vera**. A **JAK2 V617F** mutation lets the clone grow without EPO, and the high red cell mass then suppresses EPO. An EPO-secreting renal tumor is the most tempting choice, but it causes **inappropriate secondary** polycythemia with a **high** EPO. Hypoxemia (COPD, altitude) also raises EPO, and dehydration causes only relative polycythemia with a normal red cell mass.
questions.explanation_pt: Prurido após o banho, eritromelalgia, esplenomegalia, aumento das três séries, **saturação de oxigênio normal** e **EPO baixa** indicam **policitemia vera**. A mutação **JAK2 V617F** permite que o clone cresça sem EPO, e a massa eritrocitária alta então suprime a EPO. Um tumor renal secretor de EPO é a opção mais tentadora, mas causa policitemia **secundária inapropriada** com EPO **alta**. A hipoxemia (DPOC, altitude) também eleva a EPO, e a desidratação causa apenas policitemia relativa, com massa eritrocitária normal.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old woman has 6 months of fatigue, weight loss and fullness in the left upper abdomen. The spleen is massively enlarged and extends into the pelvis. Hemoglobin is 8.9 g/dL. The peripheral smear shows teardrop-shaped red cells, nucleated red cells and immature granulocytes. A bone marrow aspirate yields no material. Which finding is most likely on bone marrow biopsy?
choices: Hypocellular marrow replaced by fat
Sheets of plasma cells with eccentric nuclei
More than 20% myeloblasts with Auer rods
Ring sideroblasts with trilineage dysplasia
Reticulin and collagen fibrosis with clusters of atypical megakaryocytes
questions.explanation: Teardrop cells, a **leukoerythroblastic** smear, a **dry tap** and **massive splenomegaly** point to **primary myelofibrosis**. Clonal **megakaryocytes** release **PDGF** and **TGF-β**, which stimulate fibroblasts to fill the marrow with fibrosis; blood cells are then made in the spleen and liver (extramedullary hematopoiesis). MDS with ring sideroblasts is the most tempting choice because it also affects older adults with cytopenias, but the marrow is hypercellular and aspirates easily, and massive splenomegaly is not typical. Aplastic anemia gives a fatty marrow without splenomegaly or teardrop cells.
questions.explanation_pt: Dacriócitos (*teardrop cells*), quadro **leucoeritroblástico**, **aspirado seco** (*dry tap*) e **esplenomegalia volumosa** indicam **mielofibrose primária**. **Megacariócitos** clonais liberam **PDGF** e **TGF-β**, que estimulam fibroblastos a preencher a medula com fibrose; as células sanguíneas passam a ser produzidas no baço e no fígado (hematopoese extramedular). A SMD com sideroblastos em anel é a opção mais tentadora, pois também acomete idosos com citopenias, mas a medula é hipercelular e aspira bem, e a esplenomegalia volumosa não é típica. A anemia aplástica produz medula gordurosa, sem esplenomegalia nem dacriócitos.

notes.title: Plasma cell disorders, myeloproliferative neoplasms and MDS
notes.body_md:
## Plasma cell disorders

- **Multiple myeloma**: clonal plasma cells in the marrow of older adults. Think **CRAB**: hyper**C**alcemia, **R**enal failure, **A**nemia, **B**one lesions (punched-out lytic lesions).
- Labs: **M spike** on serum protein electrophoresis, **rouleaux**, high ESR, **Bence Jones** light chains in urine.
- Plasma cells have **clock-face** chromatin; some have red cytoplasm (**flame cells**).
- Normal antibodies are low, so bacterial **infections** are common.
- **MGUS**: an M protein without end-organ damage and fewer than 10% clonal plasma cells. It can progress to myeloma.
- **Waldenström macroglobulinemia**: monoclonal **IgM**, **hyperviscosity**, no lytic lesions.
- **AL amyloidosis**: light-chain deposits; **Congo red** with apple-green birefringence. Other amyloid types appear in the cardiomyopathy items.

## Myeloproliferative neoplasms

- Clonal stem cell disorders that make too many mature cells. **JAK2 V617F**: PV, ET, PMF. **BCR-ABL**: CML.
- **Polycythemia vera**: high red cell mass, **low EPO**, itching after bathing, erythromelalgia, **thrombosis** (including **Budd-Chiari**; see the liver block). It can progress to post-PV myelofibrosis.
- **Essential thrombocythemia**: very high platelets that work abnormally, so both **thrombosis and bleeding** occur; erythromelalgia is common.
- **Primary myelofibrosis**: marrow fibrosis, **dry tap**, **teardrop cells**, leukoerythroblastic smear, **massive splenomegaly**.
- **CML**: **t(9;22)** Philadelphia chromosome, **BCR-ABL** tyrosine kinase, massive splenomegaly, **basophilia**, **low LAP**. It can progress to **blast crisis**. Tyrosine kinase inhibitors are covered in pharmacology.
- **Leukemoid reaction**: high LAP, no basophilia, an obvious trigger such as infection.

## Sorting polycythemia

- **Relative**: low plasma volume (dehydration); normal red cell mass.
- **Primary** (PV): **low EPO**, normal oxygen saturation.
- **Secondary, appropriate**: hypoxemia (COPD, high altitude, sleep apnea); **high EPO**, low oxygen saturation.
- **Secondary, inappropriate**: EPO-secreting tumor (**renal cell carcinoma**, **hepatocellular carcinoma**); **high EPO**, normal oxygen saturation.

## Myelodysplastic syndromes

- Older adults, or after chemotherapy or radiotherapy.
- Cytopenias with a hypercellular, dysplastic marrow: **ring sideroblasts**, **pseudo-Pelger-Huët** neutrophils, fewer than 20% blasts.
- Risk of progression to **AML**.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Discrasias plasmocitárias

- **Mieloma múltiplo**: plasmócitos clonais na medula de idosos. Lembre do **CRAB**: hiper**C**alcemia, insuficiência **R**enal, **A**nemia, lesões ósseas (*B*one; lesões líticas em saca-bocado).
- Exames: **pico M** (*M spike*) na eletroforese de proteínas séricas, **rouleaux** (empilhamento de hemácias), VHS alta, cadeias leves de **Bence Jones** na urina.
- Os plasmócitos têm cromatina em **roda de carroça** (*clock-face*); alguns têm citoplasma avermelhado (**células em chama**, *flame cells*).
- Os anticorpos normais estão baixos, por isso **infecções** bacterianas são comuns.
- **GMSI**: proteína M sem lesão de órgão-alvo e com menos de 10% de plasmócitos clonais. Pode evoluir para mieloma.
- **Macroglobulinemia de Waldenström**: **IgM** monoclonal, **hiperviscosidade**, sem lesões líticas.
- **Amiloidose AL**: depósitos de cadeias leves; **vermelho Congo** com birrefringência verde-maçã. Os outros tipos de amiloide aparecem nos itens de cardiomiopatia.

## Neoplasias mieloproliferativas

- Doenças clonais da célula-tronco que produzem células maduras em excesso. **JAK2 V617F**: PV, TE, MFP. **BCR-ABL**: LMC.
- **Policitemia vera**: massa eritrocitária alta, **EPO baixa**, prurido após o banho, eritromelalgia, **trombose** (incluindo **Budd-Chiari**; ver o bloco de fígado). Pode evoluir para mielofibrose pós-PV.
- **Trombocitemia essencial**: plaquetas muito altas e disfuncionais, por isso ocorrem **trombose e sangramento**; a eritromelalgia é comum.
- **Mielofibrose primária**: fibrose medular, **aspirado seco** (*dry tap*), **dacriócitos** (*teardrop cells*), quadro leucoeritroblástico, **esplenomegalia volumosa**.
- **LMC**: **t(9;22)**, cromossomo Filadélfia, tirosina quinase **BCR-ABL**, esplenomegalia volumosa, **basofilia**, **FAL baixa**. Pode evoluir para **crise blástica**. Os inibidores de tirosina quinase estão no bloco de farmacologia.
- **Reação leucemoide**: FAL alta, sem basofilia, com um gatilho evidente, como infecção.

## Classificando a policitemia

- **Relativa**: volume plasmático baixo (desidratação); massa eritrocitária normal.
- **Primária** (PV): **EPO baixa**, saturação de oxigênio normal.
- **Secundária apropriada**: hipoxemia (DPOC, grande altitude, apneia do sono); **EPO alta**, saturação de oxigênio baixa.
- **Secundária inapropriada**: tumor secretor de EPO (**carcinoma de células renais**, **carcinoma hepatocelular**); **EPO alta**, saturação de oxigênio normal.

## Síndromes mielodisplásicas

- Idosos, ou após quimioterapia ou radioterapia.
- Citopenias com medula hipercelular e displásica: **sideroblastos em anel**, neutrófilos **pseudo-Pelger-Huët**, menos de 20% de blastos.
- Risco de evolução para **LMA**.
